title: Threat Actor Capability Matrix
description: Interactive SVG scatter plot placing five threat actor types (script kiddies, hacktivists, cybercriminals, insiders, and nation-state/APTs) on a Skill vs. Resources matrix, with circle size encoding typical campaign duration and hover tooltips for motivation, time horizon, and example incidents.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity

educational.topic: Threat actor taxonomy: skill, resources, motivation, and campaign duration
learningObjectives: Place common threat actor types on a Skill vs. Resources matrix.
Compare actors by motivation, time horizon, and example incidents.
Explain why insiders are an off-axis threat that bypasses the perimeter by design.
educational.prerequisites: Basic definitions of threat, vulnerability, and attacker motivation.

pedagogical.modelType: two-dimensional comparison scatter plot with hover reveals
controls: Hover/tap any actor circle to read motivation, time horizon, and examples
Compare positions across the Skill and Resources axes
Read the size legend mapping circle radius to campaign duration
pedagogical.assessment: Students predict where a described attacker belongs on the matrix and justify the placement using skill, resources, and duration.
misconceptionsAddressed: Assuming all attackers are highly skilled and well-resourced.
Treating insiders as just another skill/resource point rather than an access-based threat.
Equating attack severity with attacker skill rather than persistence and resources.
